verdict.rationale: Oneleet documents per-integration pages under /integrations/ for AWS (cloud, via AssumeRole), GitHub (code hosting, explicitly without access to repository contents) and Google Workspace (identity), so it covers part of a real-stack integrations catalog with some scope minimization. However, the evidence shows no HR or ticketing integrations, and its MDM is Oneleet's own product rather than a connector to a third-party MDM. Read-only scoping is only implied for GitHub and AWS, not documented as read-only. Missing for 10: HR integrations, ticketing integrations, third-party MDM connectors, explicit read-only scope documentation, a browsable catalog overview, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can connect my real stack — cloud providers, identity, HR, code hosting, MDM, ticketing — through a documented integrations catalog with read-only scopes

citations.quote: Oneleet currently monitors the following AWS resources: Accounts, RDS instances, Application and Classic load balancers, IAM users

This integration supports Cloud Security monitoring for GitHub. You can use it to monitor your GitHub configuration, user access, and Dependabot vulnerabilities. It does not require access to repository contents.
Oneleet currently monitors the following on Google Workspace: User accounts, GMail settings
Oneleet uses the AWS AssumeRole API to work with AWS resources — if you'd like to remove Oneleet's access to your workspace, simply delete the created role
